title: Going down hill
review:
I’m a longtime user of the app and have stuck with it even as it implemented the excessive number of ads because of its convenience for finding pictures and recipes, but as ai generations and influx of ads has gotten worse and worse across the app and site I find myself wanting to use it less and less. Now with the addition of an ai voice “assistant” being added in the last update I am inclined to stop using pinterest all together.

The company that owns pinterest has forgotten that pinterest is a product and that those who use it are not. Please remember that your users are your life blood and roll back some of these updates, such as the ai assistant and the use of ai in sifting through pins for removal, reduce the number of ads shown across the platform as it’s become less of an image sharing one and more of an advertisement space, and crack down on ai generated images by either implementing a more accurate means of identifying and labeling them or by allowing an image to be reported for ai usage and have a human check for legitimacy and if the image or recipe is found to be ai then to have it either tagged as such or removed.

Overall I find that Pinterest is going downhill and if things don’t change I will likely be leaving the platform permanently.

title: Algorithm is inconsistent and the comment feature is the pits
review:
I’ve used Pinterest since soon after it came out, so I have some 15 years of pins collected. Over the past six months, the algorithm has frequently become completely unusable, pulling up nothing but ads and sponsored links. Sometimes I can’t even find the different sections of my boards, rendering the organization feature completely useless. The inconsistency of the app is exasperating. Reliability matters. 

Like almost everyone else posting a critical review, I despise the ridiculous amount of AI content. 

In addition, trying to make this a social app where people can comment on other people’s pins has made this an incredibly toxic app quickly. Every time I use it, I block multiple people for their rude comments now. 

I find myself using it less and less. At this point, I assume they’re trying to tank the free version so that a paid/subscription version is palatable.

title: Illegal User Interface/Fraudulent Ad Revenue
review:
I used to love Pinterest but the app has become unusable. They changed the user interface so that you don’t have to actually press/click on an image or ad in order to open it. They have changed it to Touch Triggered Auto Open, meaning you don’t even click on a post and it automatically opens the post or advertisement. Not only does this make the app unusable because it opens every single post while trying to scroll and then you have to click out of it and go back, triggering auto refresh or losing your spot while scrolling, but this feature is also highly illegal because they do it with the intention of soliciting false ad clicks to generate fake revenue. I advise Pinterest to fix this issue as soon as possible before users start reporting their fraudulent revenue to the FTC or BBB. 

It’s one thing to deliberately change the user interface to generate fraudulent ad revenue, but it’s an entirely different thing to make it so sensitive that it makes the app unusable for even simply scrolling.

title: Mass Account Deletion
review: I never write reviews but this warrants one. My account was recently deactivated for what Pinterest says is violating community guidelines and have received an email accusing me of copyright infringement. I carefully read their polices to follow the proper steps to be heard and receive help in reactivating my account by reaching out to the Help Center. Extremely disappointing that users are being punished for using the app as the creators had intended it. Apparently this was an issue for many users last year as well and I suppose it is an issue still not resolved since it is now happening to me the same time the following year. title: With every update, they erode it a little more.
review:
The latest update has made the feed nearly unusable. Images no longer reflect my interests, and tuning the feed changes nothing. The algorithm has stopped listening. Ads have also multiplied, and none of them are relevant. The decline started when Pinterest tried to reinvent itself as a social media platform. No one comes here to gain followers or make friends. That is what Instagram and TikTok are for. Pinterest was something rarer: a focused tool for inspiration, vision boarding, and brand building. That distinction had real value. With every update, they erode it a little more.
My guidance: stop trying to be everything. The thing that made Pinterest worth recommending is still in there somewhere. Find it again.

title: Running it into the ground
review:
Over the years Pinterest has been dedicated to making their app more and more unusable, punishing their users for reblogging anything other than cooking and crafting pins, and refusing to listen to feedback. Their latest move is the nail in the coffin. Pinterest has been auto flagging pins using AI, to the point that people with no prior strikes on their accounts fully lose access to THOUSANDS of pins, to which Pinterest support shrugs and says “oh well!” 
Be warned that you could lose your account at any time for no reason. Also, their emails detailing your infractions don’t show you which pin it was, and the document attached carries a link - which doesn’t work when they deactivate the pin. So you won’t even know what it was that set off the alarm. I save fandom works and lord help you if two people are kissing or there is any skin showing. Their metric for “adult content” is puritan standards. Also I consistently get flagged for promoting self harm??? Which NONE of my pins do. AND THEY ARENT EVEN MY PINS. Email the person who UPLOADED THEM, not me!! 

I have never experienced Such dedication to alienating their long time users but they’ve consistently been making decisions that no one asks for or likes, while taking away features that were helpful and especially that actually made this place a community, for a full decade now. For no reason. The only reason people stay is because no one has made a good free alternative yet. But the time will come, Pinterest.
